body.commentary:
In some niche roles, Turkey pays higher salaries than every European country except 2-3.

Wage increases made during the cheap-financing era were a good thing — no argument there. But once financing costs spike, sustaining those raises gets a lot harder. As policy rates flow through to borrowing costs, businesses can no longer keep pace with wage growth while balancing cash flow.

There's also a composition problem: same seniority, same expertise, same role, same company profile — and pay in Turkey still outpaces most of Europe.

Does this signal a loss of skilled talent, or is it just a politically charged narrative? According to the data, this is measurable: how many people are leaving, is it 1% or 10%, and are they coming back?

How is your organization managing wage policy under today's financing cost pressure?
